claim: On 2022-07-26 AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) was renamed AWS IAM Identity Center; its features include application assignments, multi-account permissions and an AWS access portal.
question: What was IAM Identity Center called before, and when was it renamed?

evidence.quote: | [AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) renamed to AWS IAM Identity Center](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/what-is.html#renamed) | AWS introduces AWS IAM Identity Center. IAM Identity Center expands the capabilities of AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to help you centrally manage account and access to applications for your workforce users. IAM Identity Center features include application assignments, multi-account permissions, and an AWS access portal. | July 26, 2022 |

note: d011. Older questions say AWS SSO; the book names the former name once.

claim: On 2022-07-14 permission sets gained support for customer managed IAM policies and permissions boundaries, in addition to AWS managed policies.
question: Since when can IAM Identity Center permission sets use customer managed policies and permissions boundaries?

evidence.quote: | [Support for permissions boundaries and customer managed policies in permission sets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/permissionsets.html) | Added content for using AWS managed and customer managed AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies with permission sets. | July 14, 2022 |

note: d018 (date part). The rule that the policy must exist in each account is a separate fact from howtocmp.

claim: Since 2025-04-17 you can no longer provision Active Directory users with IAM Identity Center AD Sync; you use IAM Identity Center configurable AD sync instead.
question: Which feature replaced IAM Identity Center AD Sync for provisioning Active Directory users, and since when?

values.display: IAM Identity Center configurable AD Sync

evidence.quote: | [Deprecate IAM Identity Center AD Sync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/provision-users-from-ad-configurable-ADsync.html) | You can no longer provision Active Directory users with IAM Identity Center AD Sync. Instead, you can use IAM Identity Center configurable AD Sync. | April 17, 2025 |

note: d016 FRESHNESS hypothesis confirmed (date and replacement).

claim: On 2025-09-17 IAM Identity Center added support for customer managed KMS keys to encrypt workforce identity data at rest.
question: Since when can IAM Identity Center encrypt workforce identity data at rest with a customer managed KMS key?

evidence.quote: | [Customer managed keys for encryption at rest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/identity-center-customer-managed-keys) | Added support for customer managed KMS keys to encrypt workforce identity data at rest. | September 17, 2025 |

note: d015 FRESHNESS hypothesis confirmed (2025-09-17; What's New 2025-09-23 says organization instances).

claim: On 2026-02-02 IAM Identity Center added multi-Region support: replication to additional Regions, AWS account access and use of AWS managed applications in additional Regions.
question: When did IAM Identity Center become multi-Region, and what did the first release provide?

evidence.quote: | [Multi-Region support](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/multi-region-iam-identity-center.html) | Added multi-Region support, including replication to additional Regions, AWS account access and use of AWS managed applications in additional Regions. | February 2, 2026 |

note: d009 FRESHNESS hypothesis confirmed. GA before 2026-07-15, so examinable in principle; older material says IAM Identity Center lives in one Region.

claim: On 2026-07-28 multi-Region support was extended to instances that use the Identity Center directory as the identity source, in addition to external identity providers; this is after 2026-07-15, so it is not examinable yet.
question: Since when does IAM Identity Center multi-Region support work with the Identity Center directory as identity source?

qualifiers.condition: Identity Center directory as identity source

evidence.quote: | [Multi-Region support extended to Identity Center directory](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/multi-region-iam-identity-center.html) | Multi-Region support now works with the Identity Center directory as an identity source, in addition to external identity providers. | July 28, 2026 |

note: d009. Not examinable yet (RULINGS rule 7, GA after 2026-07-15).

claim: Since 2026-08-06 a new organization instance can be created with a Multi-Region option that automatically creates a customer managed KMS key and replicates the instance to an additional Region; this is after 2026-07-15, so it is not examinable yet.
question: What does the one-click Multi-Region option do when you enable a new IAM Identity Center organization instance?

values.display: automatically creating a customer managed KMS key
values.spoken: it creates a customer managed KMS key for you

evidence.quote: | [One-click multi-Region instance creation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/enable-identity-center.html) | When enabling a new organization instance in supported Regions, you can choose between Single-Region, Multi-Region, or Custom instance configurations. The Multi-Region option enables multi-Region resilience in one click by automatically creating a customer managed KMS key and replicating your instance to an additional Region. | August 6, 2026 |

claim: Since 2026-08-04 you can choose whether to enable multi-account permissions when you create an organization instance; they are enabled by default and can be enabled later; this is after 2026-07-15, so it is not examinable yet.
question: Must a new IAM Identity Center organization instance manage AWS account access?

values.display: By default, multi-account permissions are enabled

evidence.quote: | [Multi-account permissions are now optional for new instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/enable-identity-center.html) | When creating an organization instance, you can now choose whether to enable multi-account permissions. By default, multi-account permissions are enabled. You can enable multi-account permissions later from instance settings or by using the UpdateInstance API. | August 4, 2026 |

note: d014 FRESHNESS hypothesis confirmed. Not examinable yet.

claim: On 2026-06-22 IAM Identity Center began to enforce separate quotas for AWS accounts and for applications, with a new default of 7,000 for each; before, they shared a single combined quota.
question: How did the IAM Identity Center quota for AWS accounts and applications change in June 2026?

evidence.quote: | [Separate quotas for AWS accounts and applications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/limits.html) | AWS IAM Identity Center now enforces separate quotas for AWS accounts and applications. Previously, these resources shared a single combined quota. The new default quota for each is 7,000. | June 22, 2026 |

note: d013 FRESHNESS hypothesis confirmed. The old combined number is not stated in the history row; not found elsewhere.

claim: Since 2026-05-28 the guide states that permission and application access changes from group membership changes take effect immediately when new sessions are created.
question: When do group membership changes in IAM Identity Center take effect for permissions and application access?

values.display: take effect immediately when creating new sessions

evidence.quote: | [Updated authentication session timing for group membership changes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/authconcept.html) | Updated the group membership session behavior table to reflect that permission and application access changes now take effect immediately when creating new sessions. | May 28, 2026 |

note: Documentation update of the session table; see authconcept for current values.
